en: Dependent on a non-conflictive (araṇa) wholesome state, a non-conflictive unwholesome state arises by way of root condition. [Under] root [condition], one; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance [condition], one.

Dependent on a conflictive (saraṇa) unwholesome state, a non-conflictive unwholesome state arises by way of root condition. [Under] root [condition], one; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance [condition], one.
Dependent on a non-conflictive indeterminate state, a non-conflictive indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.

Conditioned by a state that is both *araṇa* and indeterminate (*abyākata*), there arises a state that is neither *saraṇa* nor indeterminate by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). There are two [answers] for the root condition ...
pe ... two for the non-disappearance condition (*avigatapaccaya*).
(The "Conascent Chapter" ... pe ... and the "Associated Chapter" are the same as the "Dependent Chapter.")

A non-conflict, indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-conflict, indeterminate state. A non-conflict, indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-conflict, indeterminate state. [There are] two [types of conditions] regarding the object;
two regarding predominance, proximity, contiguity, dependence, decisive support, prenascence, dissociation ... pe ... non-disappearance.
